```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Stachanow_2023_hydrocortisone"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Stachanow_2023_hydrocortisone"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/ph16030464> (open access; the supplement holds
  the PK/PD equations and the NONMEM code)
* Cortisol PK source: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2022.819590> (open access;
  Table 1 and the supplementary NONMEM code)

Stachanow 2023 links total plasma cortisol after a morning dose of
hydrocortisone granules (Alkindi) to 17-alpha-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP)
measured in venous dried blood spots (DBS) in young children and infants with
congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH). Cortisol inhibits the zero-order
synthesis of 17-OHP (indirect-response model, Imax = 1, Hill = 1). The PD was
fitted sequentially on top of the authors' earlier pediatric cortisol PK model
(Stachanow 2022): each child's individual PK parameters were data items. The
packaged model therefore carries the 2022 typical values and between-subject
variability for the cortisol layer, so that it can simulate new children:

* two-compartment disposition of unbound cortisol;
* saturable (Michaelis-Menten) absorption from the depot;
* saturable binding to corticosteroid-binding globulin (CBG) and linear binding
  to albumin;
* allometric weight scaling to 70 kg.

The paper used the model to derive a target range for morning DBS 17-OHP. It
simulated physiological 17-OHP from healthy children's 24-hour cortisol
profiles and multiplied the 6-8 a.m. values by 3 and by 5. That calculation is
reproduced at the end of this article.

Dosing is in **nmol** of hydrocortisone and concentrations are in **nmol/L**,
the units in which the source models were fitted. To convert a dose in mg, use
the molar mass of hydrocortisone, 362.46 g/mol (1 mg = 2759 nmol). The molar
mass is not stated in the papers.

# Population

The PK/PD model was fitted to 18 children from the phase 3 Alkindi trial
(NCT02720952; Charite Berlin): 12 young children aged 2-6 years and 6 infants
aged 28 days-2 years. They had a median age of 2.5 years (4 months-5 years)
and a median weight of 15 kg (7-21 kg) (Stachanow 2023 Table S1). The trial
enrolled 23 CAH patients and 1 patient with hypopituitarism. Each child
received one individualised morning dose of 1-4 mg (Stachanow 2022 Methods).
Plasma cortisol was sampled before the dose and at 1 h and 4 h, with two
further samples in the young children. The PD dataset had 88 venous DBS 17-OHP
concentrations, 22 of them below the LLOQ of 1.3 nmol/L; these were handled
with the M3 method. Sex and race were not reported.

The cortisol PK model (Stachanow 2022) pooled 30 dexamethasone-suppressed
healthy adults with 24 pediatric patients, including 6 neonates who are not
part of the PD cohort.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Stachanow_2023_hydrocortisone")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing at its source. They are
collected here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, 70 kg) | 400 L/h | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `lvc` (Vc, 70 kg) | 10.6 L | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q, 70 kg) | 160 L/h | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `lvp` (Vp, 70 kg) | 124 L | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `ltmax_abs` (Vmax) | 21388 nmol/h | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `lkt_abs` (Km) | 4810 nmol (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `lfdepot` (F) | 1 (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `e_wt_cl_q`, `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 Methods; supplement `$PK` |
| `lkcbg` (Kd for CBG) | 9.71 nmol/L (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `nsalb` (NSAlb) | 4.15 (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 |
| `lbs_cbg` (binding sites per CBG) | 1 (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 supplement `$THETA` 6 |
| `bmax` | `TRANSCORTIN * 1000 / 52` nmol/L | Stachanow 2022 supplement `$PK` (`CBGmol = CBG2*1000/52`) |
| `lrbase_cortisol` (pre-dose plasma cortisol) | 9.41 nmol/L | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 (`BASEchild, pla`) |
| `lkdeg` | 1.22 1/h | Stachanow 2023 Table 1 |
| `lic50` | 21.0 nmol/L | Stachanow 2023 Table 1 |
| `imax`, `hill` | 1, 1 (fixed) | Stachanow 2023 Table 1 |
| `etalcl`, `etaltmax_abs`, `etalkt_abs`, `etalfdepot` | 0.0644, 0.196, 0.270, 0.123 | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 (25.8, 46.5, 55.7, 36.1 %CV) |
| `etalbs_cbg` | 0.049 (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 supplement `$OMEGA` 6 |
| `etalrbase_cortisol` | 0.144^2 (fixed) | Stachanow 2022 supplement (`ETA(13)*THETA(14)`, omega 1) |
| `etalkdeg` | 0.0025 (fixed) | Stachanow 2023 supplement `$OMEGA`; Table 1 5.0 %CV |
| `etalic50` | 0.733 | Stachanow 2023 Table 1 (104 %CV) |
| `etalrbase` | 0.381^2 (fixed) | Stachanow 2023 supplement (`ETA(3)*THETA(3)`, omega 1) |
| `expSd` (plasma cortisol) | 0.144 | Stachanow 2022 Table 1 (14.4 %) |
| `expSd_ohp17_dbs` | 0.381 | Stachanow 2023 Table 1 (38.1 %) |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Stachanow 2022 supplement, differential equations; Stachanow 2023 supplement `$DES` |
| unbound cortisol (quadratic) | n/a | Stachanow 2022 supplement `A_u` equation; Stachanow 2023 `$DES` `AUP` |
| `d/dt(effect)`, `ksyn = rbase * kdeg` | n/a | Stachanow 2023 supplement `$PK` / `$DES` |
| `central(0)`, `effect(0)` | n/a | Stachanow 2023 supplement `A_0(2) = IBASE*V1`, `A_0(5) = OHPBASE` |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The virtual cohort below follows Table S1 and
Figure 3A of the paper:

* Weight: log-normal around 15 kg, truncated to 7-21 kg.
* CBG: 22.4 mg/L for every child. This is the value the authors used when CBG
  was not measured; the pediatric CBG distribution is not reported.
* Baseline DBS 17-OHP: log-normal with the cohort median of 14.4 nmol/L
  (Section 2.3) and a log-scale SD of 1. The SD was chosen by the maintainers
  so the draws span roughly the 3-160 nmol/L of the Figure 3A baselines.
* Dose: three arms at the trial's dose range, 1, 2 and 4 mg, given at 0 h
  (morning), with 150 children per arm.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() fixes R's draws of the covariates. rxode2's own random-effect
# draws are seeded per solver thread, so assertions below are written to hold
# for any cohort the model can produce.
set.seed(20231)
mw_hc <- 362.46 # g/mol, hydrocortisone (not stated in the source papers)
obs_times <- c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.125), seq(1.25, 4, by = 0.25), seq(4.5, 10, by = 0.5))

make_cohort <- function(n, dose_mg, id_offset = 0L) {
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(15), 0.3)), 7), 21),
    TRANSCORTIN = 22.4,
    OHP17_DBS_BL = exp(rnorm(n, log(14.4), 1)),
    dose_group = paste(dose_mg, "mg")
  )
  doses <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg * 1e6 / mw_hc, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(150, 1, id_offset = 0L),
  make_cohort(150, 2, id_offset = 150L),
  make_cohort(150, 4, id_offset = 300L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

The model has two observed endpoints (`Cc` and `ohp17_dbs`), so the
observation rows carry `dvid = 1`. Both endpoints come back as columns of
every solved row.

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Stachanow_2023_hydrocortisone"))
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("dose_group", "OHP17_DBS_BL")) |>
  as.data.frame()

mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 2, 4), function(d) {
  make_cohort(1, d, id_offset = d)
})) |>
  mutate(WT = 15, OHP17_DBS_BL = 14.4)
typ_events <- typ_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  bind_rows(
    typ_events |>
      filter(evid == 0) |>
      distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
      select(-time) |>
      tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 12, by = 0.05))
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = typ_events, keep = "dose_group") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3A: the U-shaped 17-OHP time course

The paper's Figure 3A shows observed DBS 17-OHP falling after the morning dose
and rising again as plasma cortisol declines. Most profiles reach their
minimum between about 1 and 4 h and approach baseline by 6-8 h. The
typical-value simulation reproduces that shape for a 15-kg child with the
median baseline of 14.4 nmol/L.

```{r figure-3a-typical, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_typ |>
  select(time, dose_group, Cc, ohp17_dbs) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, ohp17_dbs), names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(output = recode(output,
    Cc = "Total plasma cortisol (nmol/L)",
    ohp17_dbs = "DBS 17-OHP (nmol/L)"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = dose_group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Dose",
    caption = "Typical values, 15 kg, CBG 22.4 mg/L, baseline 17-OHP 14.4 nmol/L. Compare Figure 3A of Stachanow 2023."
  )
```

```{r u-shape-check}
u_shape <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(dose_group) |>
  summarise(
    t_nadir = time[which.min(ohp17_dbs)],
    nadir = min(ohp17_dbs),
    at_8h = ohp17_dbs[which.min(abs(time - 8))],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(u_shape |> rename(
  "Dose" = dose_group, "Time of nadir (h)" = t_nadir,
  "Nadir 17-OHP (nmol/L)" = nadir, "17-OHP at 8 h (nmol/L)" = at_8h
), digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # The nadir falls inside the 1-4 h window where Figure 3A profiles bottom out.
  all(u_shape$t_nadir > 1 & u_shape$t_nadir < 4),
  # Suppression is substantial (Figure 3A: profiles fall several-fold) ...
  all(u_shape$nadir < 0.5 * 14.4),
  # ... and the profile has recovered most of the way by 8 h.
  all(u_shape$at_8h > 0.5 * 14.4)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Neither paper reports NCA of plasma cortisol, so the PKNCA block below
documents the simulated exposure by dose group. It has no published
comparator. Cortisol is the only output where NCA applies; 17-OHP is
endogenous and is checked with the PD tests below. The pre-dose plasma cortisol
(the child's residual cortisol, 9.41 nmol/L typical) decays from time 0 and is
included in the AUC, as it is in the model.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | dose_group + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_group)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | dose_group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 10, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(dose_group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_sum |>
  rename(
    "Dose" = dose_group, "Cmax (nmol/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-10 (nmol*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated plasma cortisol NCA by dose group.")

# Saturable CBG binding makes total cortisol exposure LESS than dose
# proportional: a doubled dose frees a larger unbound fraction, which is
# cleared faster. A mis-coded binding term (e.g. linear) would give a ratio
# of about 2.
auc_ratio <- nca_sum$auclast[nca_sum$dose_group == "4 mg"] /
  nca_sum$auclast[nca_sum$dose_group == "2 mg"]
stopifnot(auc_ratio > 1.1, auc_ratio < 1.9)
```

The 4 mg / 2 mg AUC ratio is `r round(auc_ratio, 2)`, less than
dose-proportional, as expected from saturable CBG binding.

# PD and binding checks

## Binding model

The unbound amount in `model()` is the positive root of the quadratic for
saturable CBG plus linear albumin binding. At any total concentration it must
satisfy

C_total = C_u (1 + NSAlb) + Bmax C_u / (Kd + C_u).

At trace concentrations the CBG-bound share of plasma cortisol tends to
(Bmax/Kd) / (1 + NSAlb + Bmax/Kd) = 89.6 % at 22.4 mg/L CBG. Stachanow 2022
reports CBG binding of "approximately 90%" at the LLOQ, in its whole-blood
fractions.

```{r binding-check}
th <- mod$theta
kd <- exp(th[["lkcbg"]])
ns <- th[["nsalb"]]
bmax <- 22.4 * 1000 / 52
chk_bind <- sim_typ |>
  filter(dose_group == "4 mg", time > 0) |>
  mutate(
    vc = 10.6 * 15 / 70,
    cu = central_u / vc,
    resid = (cu * (1 + ns) + bmax * cu / (kd + cu)) / Cc - 1
  )
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_bind$resid)) < 1e-6)

frac_cbg_trace <- (bmax / kd) / (1 + ns + bmax / kd)
frac_cbg_peak <- with(
  chk_bind[which.max(chk_bind$Cc), ],
  bmax * cu / (kd + cu) / Cc
)
stopifnot(abs(frac_cbg_trace - 0.90) < 0.01)
```

At the 4-mg peak (`r round(max(chk_bind$Cc))` nmol/L total) the CBG-bound
fraction falls to `r round(100 * frac_cbg_peak)` %, compared with
`r round(100 * frac_cbg_trace, 1)` % at trace concentrations. Stachanow 2022
describes the same saturation.

## Steady state without cortisol

With no cortisol, `inh = 1` and 17-OHP must stay at its baseline, because
`ksyn = baseline * kdeg`.

```{r steady-state}
ev_ss <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = seq(0, 24, by = 1), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
  WT = 15, TRANSCORTIN = 22.4, OHP17_DBS_BL = 14.4
)
ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_ss, params = c(lrbase_cortisol = log(1e-8))) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(max(abs(ss$ohp17_dbs / 14.4 - 1)) < 1e-4)
```

## Figure 6: derived morning DBS 17-OHP target range

For Step C the authors drove the PD with plasma cortisol from 28 healthy
children aged 5-9 years, sampled every 20 minutes over 24 h (Figure 2). They
started the 17-OHP compartment at the median baseline of 14.4 nmol/L, ran
1000 simulations, and took the physiological DBS 17-OHP at 6-8 a.m. Those
values were multiplied by 3 and by 5 to approximate the target range. The
interquartile range of the pooled values was 2.1-8.3 nmol/L, median
4.4 nmol/L.

The individual profiles are not published. The maintainers digitised the
**median** profile (the blue line in Figure 2) at the 72 sampling times. Below,
the packaged model's PD layer is driven by that profile, with between-subject
variability on IC50 and kdeg. The PD layer is written out as an rxode2 model
whose input `CORT` is the cortisol concentration. Its parameters are read from
the packaged model, and a first check confirms it reproduces the packaged
model's 17-OHP when fed the packaged model's own cortisol.

```{r pd-only}
pd_only <- rxode2::rxode2({
  kdeg <- exp(lkdeg + etalkdeg)
  ic50 <- exp(lic50 + etalic50)
  rbase <- OHP17_DBS_BL * exp(etalrbase)
  ksyn <- rbase * kdeg
  inh <- 1 - imax * CORT^hill / (ic50^hill + CORT^hill)
  d/dt(effect) <- ksyn * inh - kdeg * effect
  effect(0) <- rbase
  ohp17_dbs <- effect
})
pd_par <- c(
  lkdeg = th[["lkdeg"]], lic50 = th[["lic50"]],
  imax = th[["imax"]], hill = th[["hill"]],
  etalkdeg = 0, etalic50 = 0, etalrbase = 0
)

# Equivalence: drive pd_only with the packaged model's own typical cortisol
# (2 mg, dense 0.05-h grid, linear interpolation) and compare 17-OHP.
drv <- sim_typ |> filter(dose_group == "2 mg")
pd_chk <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  pd_only,
  params = pd_par,
  events = data.frame(id = 1, time = drv$time, evid = 0L, CORT = drv$Cc, OHP17_DBS_BL = 14.4),
  covsInterpolation = "linear"
) |> as.data.frame()
rel_diff <- pd_chk$ohp17_dbs / drv$ohp17_dbs - 1
stopifnot(max(abs(rel_diff)) < 0.02)
```

The PD-only layer matches the packaged model within
`r signif(100 * max(abs(rel_diff)), 2)` %, the error from interpolating
cortisol linearly on the 0.05-h grid.

```{r figure-6}
# Median plasma cortisol of 28 healthy children aged 5-9 years, digitised by
# the maintainers from Figure 2 of Stachanow 2023 at the 20-minute sampling
# grid (00:00 to 23:40), nmol/L.
cort_median <- c(
  88, 153, 173, 178, 207, 212, 248, 249, 226, 217, 240, 294, 341, 345, 425, 427,
  399, 454, 455, 388, 423, 449, 500, 444, 471, 504, 408, 356, 349, 312, 310, 291,
  287, 285, 318, 288, 306, 328, 368, 362, 337, 291, 258, 227, 252, 281, 272, 260,
  224, 220, 224, 270, 220, 225, 241, 226, 187, 194, 174, 161, 131, 116, 113, 113,
  104, 92, 77, 80, 71, 70, 94, 95
)
clock <- seq(0, by = 1 / 3, length.out = length(cort_median))

n_sim <- 200
om <- mod$omega
eta_draw <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sim),
  etalic50 = rnorm(n_sim, 0, sqrt(om["etalic50", "etalic50"])),
  etalkdeg = rnorm(n_sim, 0, sqrt(om["etalkdeg", "etalkdeg"]))
)
pd_ev <- tidyr::crossing(id = seq_len(n_sim), data.frame(time = clock, CORT = cort_median)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, OHP17_DBS_BL = 14.4) |>
  left_join(eta_draw, by = "id")
pd_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  pd_only,
  params = pd_par[c("lkdeg", "lic50", "imax", "hill", "etalrbase")],
  events = pd_ev,
  covsInterpolation = "linear",
  keep = c("CORT")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

morning <- pd_sim |> filter(time >= 6, time <= 8)
target <- c(3 * morning$ohp17_dbs, 5 * morning$ohp17_dbs)
fig6 <- tibble::tibble(
  Statistic = c("25th percentile", "Median", "75th percentile"),
  `Stachanow 2023 (nmol/L)` = c(2.1, 4.4, 8.3),
  `Simulated (nmol/L)` = unname(quantile(target, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)))
)
knitr::kable(fig6, digits = 2, caption = "Derived morning (6-8 a.m.) DBS 17-OHP target range: physiological x 3 and x 5, pooled.")

# Quasi-steady state: kdeg = 1.22 1/h makes 17-OHP track cortisol within
# about an hour, so at 6-8 a.m. the solve sits close to the closed form
# baseline * IC50 / (IC50 + C) for each subject.
qss <- morning |>
  select(id, time, CORT, ohp17_dbs) |>
  left_join(eta_draw, by = "id") |>
  mutate(qss = 14.4 * exp(th[["lic50"]] + etalic50) / (exp(th[["lic50"]] + etalic50) + CORT))
stopifnot(abs(median(qss$ohp17_dbs / qss$qss) - 1) < 0.15)
```

```{r figure-6-plot, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(data.frame(target = target), aes(x = "", y = target)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, coef = 0, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1.3, 3.9), colour = "red") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 15)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time: 6-8 a.m.", y = "DBS 17-OHP morning target (nmol/L)",
    caption = "Box: IQR and median of simulated physiological x 3 and x 5.\nRed: expected range 12-36 / 9.29 (Stachanow 2023 Section 3.3)."
  )
```

The simulated range is lower than the published one: its median is about
`r round(fig6[["Simulated (nmol/L)"]][2] / 4.4, 2)` of the paper's 4.4 nmol/L.
The 17-OHP layer itself reproduces the packaged model exactly (check above), so
the gap comes from the cortisol input:

* The paper drove each simulation with one of the 28 *individual* cortisol
  profiles; only the median profile can be recovered from Figure 2.
* At quasi-steady state the morning 17-OHP is `14.4 * IC50 / (IC50 + C)`. With
  the median morning cortisol of about 450 nmol/L and IC50 = 21 nmol/L, that
  gives about 0.64 nmol/L, or a target median of about 2.6 nmol/L. The
  published 4.4 nmol/L would need a typical morning cortisol of about
  250 nmol/L, which is below the Figure 2 median between 6 and 8 a.m.

The paper does not state how the cortisol input was aligned in time or
whether the 17-OHP baseline carried its variability in Step C. The maintainers
have not been able to close the gap from the published information, and the
parameters have not been adjusted to match. The simulated range still lies in
the same order of magnitude as the paper's calculated "expected" range of
1.3-3.9 nmol/L (red lines), which was the paper's plausibility criterion.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Cortisol PK carried from Stachanow 2022.** The 2023 fit used each child's
  individual PK estimates from the 2022 model as data. The packaged model
  carries the 2022 typical values and variability (Table 1, sampling
  importance resampling medians), so it simulates new children rather than the
  fitted 18.
* **Cortisol association with red blood cells is omitted.** The 2022 model's
  RBC compartment and blood-volume term (`Vdelta`) produce DBS *cortisol*. The
  2023 PD reads total *plasma* cortisol only, so that compartment does not
  affect any output here. DBS cortisol belongs to an extraction of Stachanow
  2022 itself.
* **CBG is a covariate (`TRANSCORTIN`, mg/L).** Measured CBG was used for the
  pediatric data; when CBG was not measured the authors used 22.4 mg/L, which
  this article uses throughout.
* **Pre-dose plasma cortisol is a typical value.** The 2022 model used each
  child's observed pre-dose cortisol (or 9.41 nmol/L when unobserved), with a
  log-normal deviation whose SD equals the residual SD. The packaged model uses
  9.41 nmol/L with that deviation. The baseline is residual cortisol that
  decays from time 0 (CAH patients make little cortisol), not a steady state.
  The peripheral compartment starts empty, as in the source code.
* **17-OHP baseline is a covariate, `OHP17_DBS_BL`.** As in the source, the
  baseline is the child's observed pre-dose DBS 17-OHP, with a log-normal
  deviation whose SD equals the residual SD (`OHPBASE = BASEDV*EXP(ETA(3)*THETA(3))`,
  omega 1). Table 1 lists the "IIV on 17-OHPBASE" as 131 %CV, which is the
  unscaled omega of 1. The effective log-scale SD is 0.381. Baselines below the
  LLOQ were entered as 0.65 nmol/L.
* **Residual error read as a log-scale SD.** Table 1 reports the residual
  error, additive on the log scale, as 38.1 %CV. It is encoded as SD 0.381,
  the convention the same group's 2022 paper used (14.4 % in Table 1 = 0.144
  in its control stream). Variabilities are converted with
  omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1), which reproduces Table 1's 131.1 %CV for omega = 1.
* **Both endpoints carry a residual error.** The 2023 fit modelled only 17-OHP
  (plasma cortisol came in through the individual PK parameters). The packaged
  model also declares plasma cortisol with the 2022 residual error
  (log-scale SD 0.144), so simulated observations of both are available.
* **Below-LLOQ handling.** The M3 likelihood used for fitting does not apply
  to simulation. The LLOQ (1.3 nmol/L) is shown on the plots.
* **Virtual cohort.** CBG, the baseline 17-OHP spread and the per-arm doses
  are assumptions, as described in the Virtual cohort section.
* **Figure 6.** Driven by the digitised median cortisol profile instead of the
  28 individual profiles. The result is a lower target range than published
  (see above).
* **Errata.** No correction notice for either paper on EuropePMC
  (checked 2026-10-26).
